# Commands

`recall --help` lists the commands a person types: `init`, `sync`, `report`, `status`, `proposals`, and `config`.
`recall --help --all` also lists the commands the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts call.
A hidden command is a stable interface: it stays callable across releases, because a cron line, a config file, or a script may call it directly.
Each command's own `-h` prints its flags, shown under [Usage](#usage).

## Every command and who it is for

| Command | For | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recall init [--dry-run]` | people | set a new machine up with defaults: no bucket, scheduler, or git remote |
| `recall sync [--force]` | people | run each step that's due: imports, archive, observe, propose on the proposing machine |
| `recall report [--since 30d\|all]` | people | say what recall noticed; no model call |
| `recall status` | people | what is on, the timer and its last run, the proposing machine, pending proposals |
| `recall proposals` | people | list sent proposals and what became of them |
| `recall config show\|get\|set` | people | read and write the layered TOML config |
| `recall observe [--since 30d\|all]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | observe new or changed sessions, one model call each |
| `recall archive [--lookback N]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | upload each finished week missing from the store |
| `recall archive build WEEK OUT` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | write one week's tarball locally |
| `recall propose [--out DIR]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | fold observations into proposals and send them for review |
| `recall import [NAME...]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | fetch sessions through the import plugins config names |
| `recall lint [FILES...]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | find stale paths and commands in context files |
| `recall skills` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | report which skills sessions actually invoke |
| `recall events [PATH...]` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | print normalized transcript events as JSONL |
| `recall recur sync\|check\|list\|run` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | reconcile declared recurring jobs with cron or launchd |
| `recall hook ...` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | what the plugin's session hooks run |
| `recall extension NAME` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | print the owner's extension files for a skill |
| `recall learn ...` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | the learning loop's steps under their earlier names |
| `recall archive-chats ...` | the timer, skills, hooks, and scripts | the archive and bucket setup under their earlier names |

## Earlier spellings keep working

| Earlier spelling | Current spelling |
| --- | --- |
| `recall learn map` | `recall observe` |
| `recall learn run` | `recall propose` |
| `recall learn reviews` | `recall proposals` |
| `recall learn report` | `recall report` |
| `recall archive-chats run` | `recall archive` |
| `recall archive-chats build` | `recall archive build` |

The earlier spelling takes the same flags and runs the same step.
The other `learn` and `archive-chats` verbs keep their one spelling.
A recur job whose command runs a step under either spelling keeps the session hook from running that step too.

## Usage

The text below is each command's `recall <command> -h`.

### recall init

```text
Usage:
  recall init [--dry-run] [--backfill ask|yes|no]

Sets a new machine up with defaults that need nothing else: the store is a
local directory, proposals are reviewed on a local branch, and the plugin's
session hooks run the loop, so there is no bucket, no cron job or
LaunchAgent, no git remote, and no TOML to write by hand.

The session hooks are the default way to run the loop; recur jobs are the
opt-in for a fixed schedule. It only sets keys no config file sets yet,
through the same drop-in `recall config set` writes, and it leaves a hook
step off when a recur job's command already runs that step, so nothing runs
twice. The weekly reduce turns on only when no other machine has claimed it
on the shared store. On a machine that already has config, review stays on
pull requests, the default; init prints the command that moves it to a
local branch. With harness.claude off, each step is a recur job instead,
since Kiro's session-end hook kills the worker it would start; `recall recur sync` installs them. With
harness.kiro on, it installs the keep and recall-setup skills into Kiro CLI
as a power, from files built into this binary, so running it again after an
upgrade updates them; a missing or failing kiro-cli is a warning. Safe to
run again.

Init then offers to map the last 30 days of sessions now, showing how many
map calls that is and what they cost before it asks. On the store's reducer
the reduce and apply run right after, rather than in hooks.learn_every days;
any other machine maps only. --backfill yes maps without asking, and
--backfill no skips the offer, for scripted installs; with no input to read,
the offer is declined. Nothing else init does calls a model.
```

### recall sync

```text
Usage:
  recall sync [--force]
        run each step that is due, in order: the configured imports and
        propose on the proposing machine only, then archive and observe on
        every machine. Imports run every sync; archive uploads each finished
        week the store lacks; observe reads sessions quiet for 6 hours and
        uploads its observations; propose runs a week after its last run,
        whatever hooks.learn_every says.
        --force runs every step whether or not it is due, and observes
        sessions with no quiet period; it still never imports or proposes
        off the proposing machine.
```

### recall report

```text
Usage:
  recall report [--since 30d|all]
        say what recall noticed: the lessons the window's sessions repeat,
        then a report card of your rules; no model call.
        The same step as recall learn report.
```

### recall status

```text
Usage:
  recall status    what is on, the timer and its last run, the proposing machine,
                   and pending proposals; changes nothing and calls no model
```

### recall proposals

```text
Usage:
  recall proposals
        check what became of sent proposals (merged, closed, pending) and
        list them. The same step as recall learn reviews.
```

### recall config

```text
Usage:
  recall config show               the merged config, with where each value came from
  recall config show --defaults    every key with the value recall uses on this machine, marking the keys a file sets
  recall config get <dotted.key>   print one value (exit 1 if unset)
  recall config set <dotted.key> <value>   write one key to config.d/90-set.local.toml
```

### recall observe

```text
Usage:
  recall observe [--since 30d|all] [--limit N] [--idle 6h] [--archives] [--dry-run]
        observe new or changed sessions with learn.map_model; cached in the store.
        --idle skips a session active more recently than that, 6h by
        default; --idle 0 turns it off.
        --archives also observes archived weeks from the store.
        The same step as recall learn map.
```

### recall archive

```text
Usage:
  recall archive [--lookback N] [--dry-run [--offline]]
        upload each finished week missing from the store; the same step as
        recall archive-chats run
  recall archive build WEEK OUT
        write one week's tarball locally (WEEK like 2026-W45)
```

### recall propose

```text
Usage:
  recall propose [--out DIR] [--window 365d|all] [--force]
        sync the rules, fold the window's observations into proposals, and
        send them for review. The window defaults to learn.retire_days;
        --window reads that many days back, or every observation with all.
        --force runs on a machine that isn't the store's proposing machine,
        leaving the store ledger unwritten.
        The same step as recall learn run.
```

### recall import

```text
Usage:
  recall import [--full] [--replace] [--dry-run] [NAME...]

Runs the plugin each named harness's [harness.NAME.import] table names, and
stores the sessions it writes as that harness's (docs/import.md). With no
NAME, every enabled harness with an import table.

  --full     ask the plugin for everything, not only what changed
  --replace  accept a copy of a stored session with fewer events
  --dry-run  run the plugin and report what would change; store nothing
```

### recall lint

```text
Usage:
  recall lint [--skills-dir DIR]... [FILES...]
  recall lint --memory

Reads context files and the files they pull in through @imports and
Markdown links, and reports paths, commands, and skill names they mention
that don't exist on this machine. The default is every enabled harness's
context files: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for claude, every Markdown file under
~/.kiro/steering (AGENTS.md among them) for kiro. Exits 1 on findings.

--memory lints each harness's own memory notes instead, by the same rules,
and also reports a note its index doesn't list, an index line that points
at a missing note, and a note unchanged for longer than learn.retire_days.
It only reports; recall never edits a harness's memory.
```

### recall skills

```text
Usage:
  recall skills [--since 90d] [--skills-dir DIR]... [--json]
  recall skills --taken      every skill and command name already in use

Lists every skill it can find with how often sessions invoked it, by the
model or by slash command, and flags retirement candidates. The skill list
is the harness's own, as a session started in your home directory sees it
(plugin skills as plugin:skill), plus any --skills-dir. A project skill
counts as found when the transcript recorded where it loaded from.
```

### recall events

```text
Usage:
  recall events [--since T] [--harness NAME] [PATH...]

Prints normalized transcript events as JSONL. With no PATH, every session of
every enabled harness on this machine. A PATH is a transcript, a directory
of them, or a week's .tar.zst archive. The harness whose source directory
holds the PATH reads it, or the one --harness names. --since takes RFC 3339,
a date, or a window like 90d or 24h.
```

### recall recur

```text
Usage:
  recall recur sync         reconcile declared jobs with cron or launchd
  recall recur check        change nothing; list each job as installed and what
                            a sync would change; exit 1 on drift
  recall recur list         show the declared jobs and which file each comes from
  recall recur run NAME     run one job now, as the scheduler would
  --quiet                   with sync: print only changes, never fail
```

### recall hook

```text
Usage:
  recall hook session-start    print the repo note for the repo a session starts in
  recall hook session-end      start the loop's background work, and return at once

The recall plugin installs these as Claude Code's SessionStart and
SessionEnd hooks.

session-start reads only local files: with learn.repo_notes set, it adds the
owner's repo note for the repo the session starts in to the session's context,
and prints nothing otherwise.

session-end runs the learning loop with no cron job or LaunchAgent. The
background work does only what [hooks] in the config turns on: hooks.map,
hooks.archive, and hooks.learn_every. Its output is in
~/.local/state/recall/hook.log.
```

### recall extension

```text
Usage:
  recall extension NAME

Prints the owner's extension files for NAME (a skill name, or
learn-reduce), from extensions.NAME in config, in order. Prints nothing when
none are set. A missing file is warned about on stderr and skipped; the
command always exits 0, so a skill that injects its output never aborts.
```

### recall learn

```text
Usage:
  recall learn map [--since 30d|all] [--limit N] [--idle 6h] [--archives] [--dry-run]
        observe new or changed sessions with learn.map_model; cached in the store.
        --idle skips a session active more recently than that, so one still
        going isn't observed now and again when it grows.
        --archives also observes archived weeks from the store: other hosts'
        sessions, and this host's own that are no longer on disk; a session
        still on disk is read from disk. By default each host observes its
        own sessions and the proposing machine reads every host's
  recall learn observations [--harness NAME]
        print the cached observations as JSONL
  recall learn candidates
        list the lessons the window's sessions showed, as propose will
        read them: alike observations grouped and counted, no model call
  recall learn report [--since 30d|all]
        say what recall noticed: the lessons the window's sessions repeat,
        with session counts, dates, and your own words, then a report card
        of your rules: broken, followed, or never relevant, with counts;
        no model call
  recall learn rules sync
        reconcile the rule ledger with the bullets in learn.targets and in the
        context files of each learn.repos checkout
  recall learn targets
        list every context file and note a proposal may land in, and its scope
  recall learn age
        report rules the ledger says to reword or retire; exit 1 if any.
        Also lists, as "check", rules earned on a model no recent session
        runs, which the current model may follow unprompted
  recall learn reduce [--out DIR] [--window 365d|all] [--dry-run] [--force]
        fold the window's observations and the ledger into proposals for
        review. The window defaults to learn.retire_days; --window reads
        that many days back, or every observation with all, without
        changing retirement, which always uses learn.retire_days.
        On a machine that isn't the store's proposing machine it refuses,
        since only that machine assigns rule ids; --force runs it anyway,
        saving locally and leaving the store ledger unwritten
  recall learn apply [--from DIR] [--dry-run]
        stage a run's proposals (default: the newest) as edits in fresh
        worktrees, one per repo they touch, and send each changed repo to
        review (learn.review: a pull request or a local branch), one commit
        per proposal so a reviewer can drop one before merging
  recall learn run [--out DIR] [--window 365d|all] [--force]
        rules sync, fold into proposals, then apply: the same step as
        recall propose
  recall learn reducer [--take]
        say which host is this store's proposing machine; --take moves the
        claim to this host, for when that machine is retired, reimaged,
        or renamed
  recall learn reviews
        check what became of applied proposals (merged, closed, pending) and
        list them; propose and apply do the same check first

Observing, proposing, and applying call a model through the harness CLI
(learn.runner, claude or kiro); --dry-run builds and prints what would be
sent instead. Nothing is written to a live file: apply edits worktrees, and
every change waits for your review.
```

### recall archive-chats

```text
Usage:
  recall archive-chats run [--lookback N] [--dry-run [--offline]]  upload missing weeks
  recall archive-chats build WEEK OUT    write one week's tarball locally (WEEK like 2026-W45)
  recall archive-chats info              resolved settings and this host's uploads
  recall archive-chats check [--setup]   region, credentials, bucket, and permissions
  recall archive-chats policy setup|upload   print the IAM policy each step needs
  recall archive-chats estimate          local transcript size, compressed size, and S3 cost
  recall archive-chats setup [--dry-run] create and configure the bucket, then verify it
```
